title: About
text:
I decided to create a website focused on video game duration because players today face a real challenge: games are getting longer, bigger, and more time‑demanding, but most people have less free time than ever nowadays.
Many popular games take up to 40 or even 100+ hours to complete and players often don’t understand what they are committing to before purchasing these amazing games. I would like to help players better understand how long it actually takes to complete these games.
Across review platforms like Metacritic, both long and short games appear in the top‑rated lists. What matters most is quality, not length.

title: The Story Behind Game Playtimes
text:
HowLongToBeat is a community-driven database that crowdsources video game completion times from millions of players worldwide. Instead of relying on a single playtime estimate, the platform breaks play styles down into three core categories:

Main Story: Finishing the core objectives to see the end credits without straying into side content.
Main + Extras: Completing the main storyline while taking time to explore side quests, optional bosses, and character extras.
100% Completionist: Doing everything possible in the game—unlocking every achievement/trophy, discovering all secrets, and collecting 100% of items.

Our database contains playtime and rating metrics for over 3,100 of the most popular video games, ranging from retro classics to modern releases.

title: The Story Behind Game Playtimes
text:
Have Games Really Gotten Longer?
A frequent debate among gamers is whether modern titles demand far more time than older generations. By tracking median completion times across release years (2000–2024), we can see how game lengths have evolved across all three play styles.
Hover over any year on the chart below to inspect playtimes simultaneously, or click a style in the legend to toggle it:








Key Takeaways

Main Stories Are Remarkably Stable: For over two decades, the core campaign length of popular games has consistently hovered around 11 to 16 hours.
Completionist Time Has Surged: While the main campaign hasn’t ballooned, the depth of side content and 100% completionist runs has grown significantly with modern open-world game design.

text:
The Backlog Trap: Bought vs. Finished
Every gamer knows the feeling of buying an acclaimed title on sale, only for it to languish untouched in their backlog.
The chart below compares the number of players who completed a game against those who still have it in their backlog:

Above the dashed line: Titles where more players backlogged the game than finished it. Massive RPGs like The Witcher 3 and Fallout: New Vegas top this list.
Below the dashed line: Games with strong completion follow-through (e.g. Portal 2 and Tomb Raider).
Color: Shows story length (brighter colors indicate longer campaigns).
